subject: From note ban to 'vote ban': the mouse on the wall
alt: Satish Acharya's cartoon: on a grey wall hang two shields like hunting trophies, each with a tiny black mouse pinned to it. The left shield reads: '0.7% BLACK MONEY FOUND'. The right one reads: '1,600 FOREIGN NATIONALS OUT OF 9.86 CRORE VOTERS'. Below, the same figure with a white beard, glasses and a saffron jacket appears twice, each time raising a sword, flashing a victory sign and smiling. The left figure's sash says 'NOTE BAN' and he says: 'ZERO BLACK MONEY!' The right figure's sash says 'VOTE BAN (SIR)' and he says: 'ZERO INFILTRATORS!' The cartoonist's signature in the corner: SATISH ACHARYA.
chutki: One hunter, two trophies, and on both the same small mouse. The left shield is demonetisation, which, according to the cartoon, netted just 0.7 per cent black money. The right shield is the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the voter rolls, which turned up 1,600 foreign nationals among 9.86 crore voters. Yet below, the same victor waves his sword both times and declares: zero black money, zero infiltrators.

Satish Acharya's jab is at the habit of hanging up as a great victory the result of a drive that made the whole country stand in line, however small that result turns out to be. Notes have given way to votes, but the method is the same: dig up a mountain, and if a mouse comes out, call it a lion. The question left is on which wall the trophy will hang for the trouble crores of ordinary people went through in this hunt.
